accuracy.evidence: Definitions follow the topic's own list and standard school PSHE usage: resilience as adapting and bouncing back from adversity (APA), setback, trigger and distress as everyday terms, regulate as bringing a feeling to a manageable level rather than suppressing it (CASEL self-management), and growth versus fixed mindset as beliefs about whether ability can develop (Dweck, Mindset Works). The meter tools match NHS and Mind child guidance: slow out-breaths, naming the feeling (affect labelling) and tense-then-release, while shouting back and rumination keep feelings high.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips: resilience means never getting upset (prediction 4, mastery m1), regulating means making a feeling vanish or hiding it (prediction 2, meter floor at 1 with a note that it need not reach zero), growth mindset is just being positive (the false-growth trap in every flip, flagged by Dweck), perseverance is repeating the same approach (graph plan), a setback means failing for good (prediction 1), and trigger versus setback.

lab_distinct.evidence: Four mechanisms built for this vocabulary: word tiles dragged onto six moments of one story with definition-based bounce-back feedback, a distress meter driven by dragged tools, a fixed-to-growth thought flipper with a cheerful decoy, and a bounce-back graph where weekly plans set the line. It shares no mechanics with the 5 to 6 persisting lab (beanbag, bike wobble, tower) or the big-feelings lab, and its code is under the 30 percent similarity limit.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each word is met in context before it is named: the wrong-drop feedback contrasts two definitions, the meter shows that some tools push the feeling up, the flipper shows that cheerful is not growth, and the graph shows only keeping going with a new way reaches 25 m (7 + 4 x 5 = 27, while the same way again reaches only 15). The step text confirms after the action.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options: a setback as the end, regulate as make it go away for ever or hide it, growth mindset as always feeling happy, and resilience as never getting upset or failing. Each is followed by a task that shows the opposite on the canvas.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Nine rotating scenarios, each with two plausible distractors. Wrong answers get feedback that names the slip: trigger versus setback, persevere as the keep-going part versus resilience as the whole bounce back, what a thought says about change for growth versus fixed, and a definition-to-definition contrast otherwise. A glossary on the canvas highlights the right word after each answer.

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs use short sentences and one example per word for ages 7 to 10, within the kid readability limit; the adult text passes the 9.5 grade limit. Tiles are one or two words, story moments are one sentence, and feedback is one or two short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence defines a word, gives an example or checks one. The adult text names the mistakes and a concrete home routine. There is no greeting, scene-setting or praise padding in the lesson or the lab copy.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots: story moments sit in a two-column grid with full-text wrapping, word tiles are 46 px tall, the meter tools wrap two per row under a meter that keeps its height, thought options and weekly plans are full-width 46 px buttons, and the challenge glossary wraps within the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a button twin: pick-a-word then put-on-moment buttons, one button per meter tool plus reset, one per thought option, and one per weekly plan plus start again. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with placed words, distress level or the weekly distances, and the walkthrough reports axe clean in both themes.
